name: Turn-around speed
summary: Give turning around its own, stronger acceleration so reversing is quick even when stopping is gentle.
what_it_does: Many controllers use the stopping deceleration when the player reverses, so a soft stop also means a slow, skidding turn. Splitting the turn out gives one more knob: when input points against the current speed, use a separate, larger turn acceleration. The character keeps its gentle stop and still changes direction quickly.
use_when: Characters that should feel nimble but not stop on a dime.
watch_out: A heavy character with a deliberate skid wants the slow turn.
starting_values: No checked source gives a separate turn number. Game Maker's Toolkit notes that Madeline changes direction very quickly with no skidding, and Celeste's code uses its full run acceleration when turning. Try 2 to 3 times your normal acceleration.
prompt:
Give turning its own acceleration.
- When horizontal input points opposite to the current horizontal speed, move speed toward the target at 4000 px/s² instead of the normal deceleration.
- Stopping with no input still uses the normal deceleration.
- Optional: spawn skid dust while turning.

Acceptance checks:
1. Reversing from full speed takes less time than before. Log both.
2. Releasing input still slides to a stop as before.
3. Same result at 30 and 144 fps.
